messages:
sam: heads-up — saw a spike in pod evictions on the gpu-ephemeral nodegroup during the 03:20 maintenance window; ~12 pods got rescheduled and we had a ~20% traffic tail increase for the realtime endpoint. Not a full incident but enough to ping on cost/strategy tradeoffs.
jia: thanks for flagging. are these the mixed-capacity nodes (ephemeral + reserved) or a pure ephemeral pool?
sam: mixed-capacity. pattern looks like the ephemeral instances got reclaimed but CA then immediately spun up new ephemeral nodes which caused a bunch of churn + scheduling latency.
omar: curious — did CA scale-down/scale-up overlap with our termination hook? we added the lifecycle hook that should mark nodes as NoSchedule for new pods for 60s before drain.
sam: lifecycle hook fired, but the kubelet was still accepting new pods until the termination probe finished. result: new pods landed -> got moved.
priya: ah, that's the race I feared. We currently rely on a cloud preemption notice handler that sets a taint: "ephemeral/preempting:NoSchedule" and then triggers graceful-drain script. But if CA sees capacity shortfall, it scales up before taint fully propagates.
kevin: ops idea: introduce a node state "suspend" where node reports Ready=false for scheduling but doesn't initiate eviction. CA and scheduler would treat it as drained for scheduling decisions but not force pod moves until lifecycle hook completes. That reduces churn when ephemeral nodes are reclaiming.
maria: we prototyped something similar in a sandbox: marking the node with a taint + extended taint-duration prevented new pods landing for ~45s and CA paused replacement launch, net fewer reschedules. downside: small capacity hole that slightly increases latency for a short period.
priya: alternative is to make CA prefer reserved capacity for immediate replacement during preemptions — that is, on signal route requests to reserved pools for hot paths instead of spin-up ephemeral. Could tie routing to pod annotations / nodeSelector.
jia: does anyone have metrics on cost delta if we route more to reserved for short durations? I want an order-of-magnitude estimate before we change autoscaler policy.
omar: rough: reserved is ~2.8x cost per GPU-hour vs ephemeral, but if we only failover for <3 minutes and reduce churn, net token-cost savings because we avoid double-scheduling + warmup. ballpark savings depend on request rate.
kevin: engineering tradeoff: implementing "suspend" requires changes in node-prober + cloud lifecycle handler + CA admission hook. Could be incremental: first adjust the preempt handler to set a long NoSchedule taint early, then teach CA to treat nodes with "ephemeral/pending-drain=true" as non-existent for scale decisions.
sam: propose short RFC: 1) extend preempt handler to set taint asap on notice arrival; 2) add a cloud hook to delay node termination until pods reach terminal state or PDBs satisfied; 3) change CA to ignore nodes with the taint when calculating needed replicas for 90s.
maria: +1. also suggest a metric to track: reschedule_count_per_preempt, avg_pod_start_latency_during_preempt, extra_tokens_per_preempt_window.
priya: small operational note: any change must respect PDBs — we cannot extend drain time too long if PDBs block it.
jeff (infra-bot): deploy-checks: lint:pass, unit-tests:fail (1), canary:pending.
kevin: who can take the preempt handler taint-time change? I'll pick up the CA change if someone owns the cloud hook.
omar: I can draft the cloud lifecycle hook (AWS/GC specific) and test in sandbox.
jia: I'll run cost sims with historical preempt traces to model reserved-fallback vs suspend. give me 48 hours.
sam: thanks. for the RFC, please include the small example snippet we used in sandbox: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Node metadata: labels: node.kubernetes.io/ephemeral: "true" spec: taints: - key: "ephemeral/preempting" value: "true" effect: "NoSchedule" ```
priya: logging + observability: add a metric that increments when preempt handler sets the taint and annotate traces with preempt_id so we can correlate request tails.
maria: can we also add a fast fallback in the router: if a pod is on an endpoint getting a preempt taint event, route new requests away for 30s while we stabilize? probably need app-level support.
kevin: ok. actionables: Omar drafts lifecycle hook (owner), Kevin implements CA ignore rule, Jia runs cost sims, Maria wires observability, Priya updates preempt handler and PDB guard. I'll create a short RFC doc and link it here.
sam: awesome — thanks everyone. ping @oncall if we see this at scale tonight. :thumbsup:
